position_a: External focus superior for performance, retention and transfer (g=0.264 / 0.583 / 0.584)
position_b: Bias-corrected reanalysis returns a null; effect may be inflated by small-study and publication bias
evidence_a: Chua et al. 2021 meta-analysis, 73 studies / 1824 participants (doi 10.1037/bul0000335, PMID 34843301)
evidence_b: McKay et al. 2024 robust Bayesian bias-corrected meta-analysis
adjudication: UNRESOLVED IN THE LITERATURE. Do not present external focus as settled science. The practical cost of using external cues is near zero and the downside risk is low, so it remains a reasonable DEFAULT — but it must be labelled CONTESTED, not evidence-based.
ppbf_action: Cue library ships with focus_type tagged and a CONTESTED banner. No SHADOW scoring or ranking of cues by focus type. Candidate for PPBF's own A/B retention test.

position_a: High contextual interference improves retention (54 studies) and transfer (SMD=0.55, 34 studies)
position_b: Null in one systematic review; only 20% of 183 outcomes favoured high CI in an applied 2024 review
adjudication: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The dissociation between practice performance and retention is robust and is the single most important coaching principle in this program. The MAGNITUDE and the applied-setting generalisation are contested.
ppbf_action: Teach the acquisition/retention dissociation as doctrine. Do not ship a numeric 'optimal interference' parameter. Session templates offer blocked-to-random progression as an option, not a prescription.

position_a: Faded/reduced feedback frequency improves learning — the rule most coaches were taught
position_b: Meta-analytic null: no significant effect at any time point, no acquisition-to-retention crossover
evidence_b: McKay et al. 2022, 61 papers, k=75, N=2228 (doi 10.1016/j.psychsport.2022.102165)
adjudication: RESOLVED AGAINST THE TRADITIONAL RULE. This is a 'coaches should stop doing this' item — specifically, stop believing that withholding feedback is itself beneficial.
ppbf_action: Remove any feedback-frequency prescription from session templates and SHADOW guidance. Feedback QUALITY and athlete control are better-supported levers than frequency.

position_a: Meta-analytic retention and transfer benefit from learner-controlled feedback
position_b: Trivial effects in golf putting; preregistered replication failure for the retention benefit of choice
adjudication: CONTESTED as a motor-learning effect. HOWEVER autonomy support has independent and stronger support in the motivation/adherence literature (SDT), which is a different outcome.
ppbf_action: Justify autonomy-supportive coaching on ADHERENCE and coach-athlete relationship grounds (well supported), not on motor-learning grounds (contested). This distinction must appear in the coach education material.

topic: Aggression: does boxing increase or decrease it?
position_a: Martial arts participation reduces anger/aggression
position_b: Power-sport participation associated with antisocial/aggressive outcomes in a longitudinal cohort
evidence_a: Systematic review, mixed findings (doi 10.1016/j.avb.2021.101611); Nosanchuk 1981/1989 traditional-training effect
evidence_b: Longitudinal Norwegian cohort, male-only, power sports
adjudication: GENUINELY BIDIRECTIONAL. Moderators (traditional vs modern instruction, coach behaviour, climate) are the plausible mechanism but are not established for boxing.
ppbf_action: PROHIBITED CLAIM: PPBF marketing, grant applications and the app must NOT state that boxing reduces aggression. Permitted statement: evidence is mixed and program design likely matters. This is a governance rule, added to the claim-review gate.

position_a: ACWR is a usable injury-risk monitoring tool
position_b: ACWR is statistically flawed — coupling produces spurious correlation, thresholds are arbitrary
evidence_b: PMID 29101104 (coupling/spurious correlation); PMID 31672926 and related critiques
adjudication: CONTESTED, LEANING AGAINST. The critique is methodological and has not been rebutted at the level it was made.
ppbf_action: SHADOW must NOT compute an ACWR threshold or a risk flag from it. Log raw load; display trend and monotony descriptively with n visible. Capability module 022 (Injury Risk Engine) and 014 (Load Management) must be re-scoped to descriptive monitoring. Added to do-not-build-yet.
status: RESOLVED — DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS DECISION RULE

position_a: Neck strengthening reduces concussion risk — widely promoted in combat sport
position_b: Meta-analysis found no significant strength differences across five planes; 3 of 2462 papers had injury outcomes, none showed protection
adjudication: RESOLVED AGAINST THE PROTECTIVE CLAIM. Neck training may be justified for other reasons (performance, tolerance of routine loading) but not as concussion prevention.
ppbf_action: PROHIBITED CLAIM. Neck work may appear in programming; the app and coach material must not attribute concussion protection to it.

position_a: Laboratory biomechanics show headguards reduce linear head acceleration (~130g bare vs ~85g with headguard)
position_b: Stoppages due to head blows DECREASED after headguard removal; ringside physicians state headguards should not be relied on for concussion prevention
evidence_b: PMID 27116592 with response letter PMID 27740948; Association of Ringside Physicians position (A5)
adjudication: ACTIVELY CONTESTED AND JURISDICTION-DEPENDENT. Laboratory attenuation of linear acceleration does not equal concussion prevention in competition; headguards may alter behaviour and target profile.
ppbf_action: PPBF follows the governing body rule for the division, full stop. The app stores headguard requirement as DATED REFERENCE DATA per jurisdiction/division, never as a computed safety recommendation. No PPBF claim that headguards prevent concussion.

position_a: Consensus neuropathological criteria establish CTE as a distinct pathological entity
position_b: Published argument that 'CTE is not a real disease' as a clinical syndrome
adjudication: SPLIT THE CLAIM. Pathology in exposed populations: established. Individual-level clinical prediction from exposure: not established. Both rows retained deliberately in the registry.
ppbf_action: PPBF may state that repeated head impacts carry long-term risk and that reducing unnecessary head contact is prudent. PPBF must NOT estimate any individual's CTE risk, and SHADOW must never compute one. Head-impact exposure is logged as a countable proxy only.

topic: ISSN weight-cutting position stand vs PPBF policy
position_a: The 2025 ISSN position stand describes acute weight-loss methods (sauna, hot water immersion, wraps, water loading) as practices to be managed
position_b: PPBF's youth and community context requires prohibition, and the youth RWL literature recommends banning the practice in this population
evidence_b: Youth RWL systematic reviews; PMID 30299200 (only 3.5% of participants female)
adjudication: NOT A SCIENTIFIC CONFLICT — A SCOPE CONFLICT. The position stand addresses adult professional/elite combat athletes with medical supervision. PPBF's population is youth and community adults without that infrastructure.
ppbf_action: PPBF policy prohibits youth weight cutting outright and does not provide adult cutting protocols. The weight_management_safety_policy.md draft must state explicitly that it DEPARTS from the ISSN stand on scope grounds, and why — so the departure is documented rather than looking like ignorance of the literature.

position_a: The AAP and Canadian Paediatric Society jointly OPPOSE boxing participation by children and adolescents
position_b: PPBF operates a youth boxing program
adjudication: MATERIAL GOVERNANCE CONFLICT — the most consequential one in this program. It cannot be resolved by research and must not be buried.
ppbf_action: ESCALATE TO BOARD AND MEDICAL ADVISOR. PPBF must adopt a written, board-approved position that acknowledges the AAP/CPS statement by name, states PPBF's risk-mitigation posture (non-contact entry lane, contact gating, exposure minimisation, medical oversight), and is disclosed to parents at intake. Do not proceed with youth contact expansion until this exists.

position_a: An operational ratio is needed for capacity planning and dominates program economics
position_b: No verified coach:athlete ratio exists for boxing or any combat sport in the searched literature
evidence_a: B5: supervision ratio swings annual surplus by ~$42,930 at a 100-athlete roster
evidence_b: B1-047, B3-058, B6-150 all INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
adjudication: NO EVIDENCE EXISTS. The only numeric anchors located are PA child care licensure (1:12 young school-age, 1:15 older school-age, max group 24/30, 55 Pa. Code 3270.51) which is NOT a sport standard and NOT a boxing standard.
ppbf_action: PPBF sets supervision ratios as a written SAFETY POLICY decision owned by the Head Coach and board, informed by insurer requirements and USA Boxing sanctioning terms — not by this research. Every ratio in the capacity and finance models is a labelled parameter, never a recommendation. Risk-tiered by activity (open sparring tightest).
status: RESOLVED AS POLICY DECISION, NOT RESEARCH OUTPUT

position_a: pilot.attendance records athlete-day participation
position_b: pilot.scheduler_attendance records class-level participation
evidence_a: Both tables exist in the live schema
adjudication: SCHEMA DEFECT, NOT A RESEARCH CONFLICT. Every funder-facing and board-facing participation figure is currently at double-count risk.
ppbf_action: Declare ONE authoritative attendance source in writing before any KPI ships. Recommendation: pilot.attendance as the athlete-day system of record, scheduler_attendance as the class-session detail feeding it, with a documented reconciliation view. Blocking dependency for the entire KPI layer.

topic: Medical determination vs coaching contact permission
position_a: pilot.shadow_medical_administrative_status is the only home for restriction state
position_b: A clinician's medical determination and a coach's contact permission are different decisions with different owners
evidence_b: Authority model requires distinct decision owners
adjudication: CONFLATION DEFECT. Storing both in one field means the system cannot represent 'medically cleared but not yet coach-approved for contact', which is the normal state for a returning or novice boxer.
ppbf_action: Split into two entities with separate owners, timestamps and audit trails: medical_clearance_status (owner: qualified medical professional, SHADOW OBSERVE-ONLY) and contact_authorisation (owner: Head Coach, SHADOW OBSERVE-ONLY). Neither may be computed.

position_a: pilot.athletes.emergency_contact holds a contact
position_b: pilot.emergency_contacts is a separate table
adjudication: TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR A SAFETY-CRITICAL FIELD. In an emergency the wrong one may be read.
ppbf_action: Consolidate to pilot.emergency_contacts; deprecate the column with a migration and a read-path audit. Safety-critical, so this ranks above feature work.

topic: Instrumented head-impact sensors vs human video coding
position_a: Instrumented mouthguards/patches give objective head-impact exposure
position_b: Sensor data quality in boxing is poor: criteria met in only 53% (mouthguard), 20% (skin patch), 26% (headgear patch) of 442 sparring events; sensitivity against 5168 video-identified events was 35%/86%/7%
evidence_a: Sensor vendor and general HIE literature
evidence_b: A5 and A8 both verified this independently
adjudication: RESOLVED. Human video coding currently outperforms wearable sensors for counting head contacts in boxing. Sensors are not a shortcut.
ppbf_action: PPBF uses COUNTED PROXIES (sparring rounds by intensity category, coach-observed impacts) with their validity limits stated. Do not purchase head-impact sensors as a measurement solution. Inter-rater reliability on the video count is the binding constraint to invest in.

position_a: Diversification improves nonprofit financial stability
position_b: Concentration has rewards; grant dependence may be the real driver; diversification carries execution cost
adjudication: GENUINELY UNRESOLVED in the nonprofit finance literature, and all of it transfers from non-boxing (largely German Verein-form) contexts.
ppbf_action: Do not set a diversification target as a KPI. Track revenue concentration descriptively alongside the IRS public support test requirement, which is a hard compliance constraint rather than a strategy preference.

position_a: A single cost-per-athlete figure is wanted for board and funder reporting
position_b: There is no single correct definition — denominator and cost allocation choices change it substantially
adjudication: RESOLVED AS A DEFINITIONAL REQUIREMENT. Any single figure without its denominator is a vanity metric.
ppbf_action: PPBF must choose and WRITE DOWN one denominator (recommend: unique athletes with >=1 attended session in the period) and one cost-allocation rule, and display both with every figure. Enforced by the dashboard honesty spec.

position_a: NFHS/NCAA exclusion thresholds (72h topical antifungal tinea; 120h oral antiviral herpes gladiatorum; 72h post-I&D MRSA) are the operative standard
position_b: These are wrestling-derived, where skin-to-skin exposure is far higher than boxing
adjudication: TRANSFER IS CONSERVATIVE AND ACCEPTABLE. Applying a stricter-than-necessary exclusion standard errs toward safety; the reverse would not.
ppbf_action: Adopt the wrestling-derived thresholds explicitly LABELLED as transferred, and route every exclusion decision to a qualified health professional rather than a coach or the app.

topic: Jurisdictional divergence on minimum contact age
position_a: England Boxing prohibits sparring under 10
position_b: USA Boxing registers competitors from age 8 with Prep sub-divisions
adjudication: NOT A CONFLICT TO RESOLVE — A PARAMETERISATION REQUIREMENT. Both are correct in their jurisdictions.
ppbf_action: All contact/sparring age logic must be parameterised by sanctioning body and jurisdiction as dated reference data with a retrieval date and a human re-verification cadence. Never hardcode an age.

position_a: LTAD is the dominant youth athlete development framework and is widely adopted
position_b: LTAD is one-dimensional, lacks empirical basis, and rests on questionable assumptions; the strongest participation-pattern evidence inverts the intuitive early-specialisation pathway
adjudication: CONTESTED. Adoption is not evidence. The diversification-over-early-specialisation direction has better support than the staged-model specifics.
ppbf_action: PPBF may use stage LANGUAGE for communication but must not implement LTAD stage boundaries as gating logic or as computed readiness. Progression gates are competency- and safety-based, human-approved.

position_a: Rear hook produces highest force (2624+/-581 N, senior elite amateurs)
position_b: Cross produces highest force (1475.42 N, dual force plates plus boxing manikin)
adjudication: METHOD-DEPENDENT AND NOT RESOLVABLE from current data. Measurement apparatus differs so fundamentally that the values are not comparable.
ppbf_action: No PPBF material may rank punches by force. No app feature may score or compare punch power across athletes or punch types. Consumer punch trackers showed no strong correlation with criterion measures and must not be used for assessment.

topic: Session-RPE as PPBF's internal load foundation
position_a: Session-RPE is the practical internal-load measure and is well validated in sport generally
position_b: A boxing-specific session-RPE study now exists: 8 boxers, matched-pairs randomized, three standardized intensities. Session-RPE at 10 min did not differ significantly from 30 min at easy (1.3±1.0 vs 1.7±1.0 AU), moderate (2.7±1.6 vs 2.5±0.9 AU) or hard (5.7±1.0 vs 5.8±1.9 AU).
evidence_b: PMID 24570606 (Penn State full text, extracted and verified 2026-08-08)
adjudication: REVISED 2026-08-08. The original framing — that PPBF's internal-load foundation rested entirely on transfer from karate and taekwondo — is no longer accurate. One boxing-specific study establishes that the session-RPE measurement window is forgiving in boxers: 10 min and 30 min post-session give statistically indistinguishable values across easy, moderate and hard sessions. This does NOT validate session-RPE against internal load in boxing generally (n=8, one squad, adult male, no youth or adaptive participants).
ppbf_action: Adopt session-RPE with a 10-30 minute collection window; the app must not penalize or down-weight entries anywhere in that window. PPBF's validation study is still warranted but is re-scoped: no longer 'establish session-RPE in boxing from scratch' but 'extend an existing boxing finding to youth, female and adaptive athletes, and test against an internal-load criterion'.
status: REVISED — BOXING ANCHOR NOW EXISTS; VALIDATION RE-SCOPED

position_a: Capability modules 022 (Injury Risk Engine) and related propose injury risk scoring
position_b: FMS composite has poor predictive value across 24 appraised studies; Y-Balance similar; no validated individual injury prediction exists
adjudication: RESOLVED AGAINST. No validated individual injury prediction exists in this domain.
ppbf_action: Module 022 must be re-scoped from prediction to descriptive exposure monitoring, or moved to do-not-build-yet. SHADOW must not output an injury risk score. This is a prohibited automated decision.

position_a: A Hand Clinics review asserts clear evidence that hand protection reduces hand injury
position_b: No controlled trial of hand-wrap injury prevention in boxing was located
adjudication: CONTESTED. Wrapping rests on mechanical reasoning, governing-body MANDATE and tradition — not trial evidence. The mandate alone is sufficient reason to wrap correctly; the evidence claim is not.
ppbf_action: PPBF and SHADOW must NEVER claim wrapping prevents injury. Justify the SOP on rule compliance and mechanical reasoning. The hand is nonetheless the most-injured location (302 injuries/1000 competition hours, GB squad), so the SOP matters regardless of the claim.

position_a: A single correct wrap length/spec can be taught
position_b: Four incompatible amateur standards (USA Boxing 8.2-14.76 ft; England Boxing 2.5-4.5 m; World Boxing 3.5-4.5 m x2; Boxing Canada max 2.5 m) and two incompatible US professional standards (Michigan 10-12 yd; Indiana 20 yd gauze)
adjudication: NO UNIVERSAL STANDARD EXISTS. This is dated reference data per sanctioning body, not a teachable constant.
ppbf_action: The app must render wrap specification from a jurisdiction/division reference table with retrieval dates and a human re-verification cadence. Never hardcode a length. The SOP teaches METHOD; the spec comes from the rulebook in force.

position_a: The app could checklist and confirm a wrap
position_b: Every jurisdiction examined assigns wrap approval to a designated HUMAN official who signs or seals the wrap
evidence_b: A6-077, EQ-031 across USA Boxing, England Boxing, World Boxing, WBC Amateur, Michigan, Indiana
adjudication: RULE-DERIVED HARD BOUNDARY. Not a design preference.
ppbf_action: SHADOW may RENDER the checklist and record that a named official signed. SHADOW must NEVER certify, approve, or imply a wrap is safe or compliant. Added as a PROHIBITED row in the authority matrix.

position_a: Gauze-and-tape wrapping is standard professional practice
position_b: World Boxing MANDATES the simpler Velcro bandage for U17/U19 and restricts gauze-and-tape to Elite
adjudication: RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE RESTRICTION. This is the strongest youth-safety precedent located in the wrapping domain.
ppbf_action: PROPOSED PPBF POLICY P1: no gauze-and-tape under 19, mirroring World Boxing. Labelled PROPOSED PPBF PARAMETER pending coach-lead and board sign-off.

position_a: USA Boxing requires headgear for ALL divisions
position_b: England Boxing and World Boxing exempt senior/elite MEN
adjudication: BOTH CORRECT IN THEIR JURISDICTIONS. Never present either as universal. Note this is a separate question from whether headguards prevent concussion (CT-08).
ppbf_action: Headgear requirement is dated reference data keyed to sanctioning body, division, age and sex. The app renders the rule in force; it does not reason about it.

position_a: A standard corner kit can be specified
position_b: World Boxing permits only adrenaline 1/1000 and non-petroleum jelly; USA Boxing permits a much longer named list; England Boxing restricts application to an accredited individual
adjudication: GENUINE JURISDICTIONAL CONFLICT with safety and eligibility consequences.
ppbf_action: The corner card must be GENERATED PER SANCTIONING BODY from reference data, never from a generic kit list. Application of any agent remains with the accredited human. SHADOW renders, never advises.

position_a: PA child care licensure gives 1:12 (young school-age) and 1:15 (older school-age)
position_b: UK safeguarding guidance gives tighter ratios: 1:8 ages 9-12, 1:10 ages 13-18 (NSPCC)
evidence_a: 55 Pa. Code 3270.51 — not a sport standard
evidence_b: NSPCC Sport, The FA Guidance 5.5 v1.3
adjudication: NO BOXING RATIO EXISTS IN EITHER SYSTEM. The applicable law is US; the clearest numeric guidance is UK. NSPCC itself states sport-specific NGB guidance should take precedence and usually requires MORE adults.
ppbf_action: B2 adopts the TIGHTER (UK) value as the proposed floor, with the PA licensure figures recorded as the legal reference and the two-adult minimum (converging across 55 Pa. Code 3270.54, NSPCC Sport and The FA) as the hard floor. All labelled PROPOSED, owned by Head Coach and safeguarding lead. Supersedes any single-jurisdiction anchor.
status: RESOLVED — TIGHTER VALUE ADOPTED AS PROPOSED FLOOR

topic: Queueing model choice for pad work
position_a: A waiting-time estimate can be shown to coaches
position_b: Model choice spans two orders of magnitude for the same 25-athlete class: deterministic rotation ~1.2 min; finite-source ~64 min at 1 pad coach; M/M/c unstable below 4 pad coaches
adjudication: RESOLVED AS A DISPLAY RULE. The spread between defensible models IS the finding; a single number would be false precision.
ppbf_action: SHADOW must never emit a single waiting-time number. Present the range with the model assumption named, or present nothing. Feeds the dashboard honesty spec.
status: RESOLVED — RANGE ONLY, NEVER A POINT ESTIMATE

topic: Pad-contact minutes as a learning proxy
position_a: The throughput model optimises coach contact minutes as the scarce resource
position_b: Motor-learning evidence cautions against equating contact minutes with learning: feedback-frequency effects are a meta-analytic null, and the contextual-interference benefit appeared on delayed transfer at 40 days, not acute performance
adjudication: BOTH VALID — DIFFERENT OBJECTIVES. Contact minutes are a SUPERVISION and OPPORTUNITY measure, not a learning measure.
ppbf_action: Capacity planning may optimise contact minutes. The app must NOT display contact minutes as a learning or progress metric, and SHADOW must not recommend more pad time as a development intervention on throughput grounds. Added to the dashboard honesty spec.

topic: Post-knockout rest periods as a capacity constraint
position_a: Sparring rosters can be planned from availability
position_b: USA Boxing post-knockout rest periods (30/90/365 days) apply to SPARRING as well as competition
adjudication: RESOLVED. These are hard eligibility constraints on the sparring roster, not soft planning inputs.
ppbf_action: Modelled as a HUMAN-ENTERED administrative flag only. SHADOW may DISPLAY the flag and its expiry date; it must never compute, infer, or clear a rest period. Medical and eligibility authority remains human.

topic: Post-activation potentiation as a prescribable protocol
position_a: PAPE protocols improve subsequent power output and could be prescribed as a standard pre-session potentiation block
position_b: In boxers the effects are small and individual: worthwhile changes only, RFD gains limited to the cross, and 6 of the boxers responded best to one protocol while others did not. In a separate study the SAME back-squat conditioning activity significantly INCREASED peak torque in one measure and significantly DECREASED peak torque and average power in another.
adjudication: RESOLVED AGAINST PRESCRIPTION. PAPE is real but response is individual and site-specific — the same conditioning activity potentiates one capacity while impairing another in the same athletes. A single prescribed protocol would help some athletes and degrade others, and nothing in this evidence identifies who is who in advance.
ppbf_action: PAPE may be offered as a coach-selectable warm-up option with the individual-response caveat displayed. SHADOW must NOT recommend a potentiation protocol to a named athlete, and must not infer responder status from performance data. Add to the do-not-build-yet list.

topic: Warm-up decay across an inactive gap
position_a: A warm-up completed before a session carries through the session
position_b: In elite boxers a standardized warm-up produced a 4.8% increase in countermovement jump height, and a 25-minute inactive gap between warm-up and boxing activity produced decreases in CMJ height and upper-body power.
adjudication: RESOLVED. Warm-up benefit decays measurably across an inactive gap. This is one of the few findings in the batch that is boxing-specific, directional and actionable without further validation.
ppbf_action: Add a universal stop-rule / script-block rule: where more than ~20 minutes elapses between warm-up and working effort — waiting for a ring, bout delays, late class start — re-warm before contact or maximal work. Implement as coach guidance, bypassable with a note like every other flag.
